location: ul-it-policy/technical/ch01-synthesis-EN.tex § How to use the rest of the Technical Reference (sec:synth-using), \paragraph heading line 541
proposedGenericDecision: Replace the institution-shaped governance body name 'rectorate' with a role-based label for the top-level academic/executive governance body (e.g., 'senior governance body' / 'executive governance').
rationale: 'Rectorate' is the governance-shape term used by continental European / civil-law universities (and is the UL form). Anglophone and federated systems use 'board of trustees', 'board of governors', 'president's office', 'governing council'. This is an IMPLICIT governance-shape assumption that binds the document to a rectorate-style institution. A role-based label ('senior governance body') is institution-agnostic.

surfaceForm: the institutional governance bodies that mandate them
proposedGenericDecision: Already role-based ('institutional governance bodies'); keep. No single governance shape is presupposed here.
rationale: Phrasing is already abstract and role-based; it does not name a rectorate/board/senate. Recorded as keep so the matrix shows this was reviewed and intentionally left, contrasting with the 'rectorate' occurrence on line 541.

location: ul-it-policy/technical/ch01-synthesis-EN.tex § Migration playbook (sec:synth-migration) line 332-333; repeated in Self-assessment (sec:synth-self-assessment) line 495
proposedGenericDecision: The trajectory names a specific proprietary vendor stack. For an institution-agnostic suite, parameterize to the dominant-proprietary-suite trajectory (role: 'incumbent proprietary productivity/identity suite') or name the vendor only as an illustrative instance.
rationale: 'Microsoft-centric' is a concrete vendor binding. It is widely representative (many universities run M365/Entra), so dropping it loses signal; but a truly vendor-neutral framing would describe the trajectory by role ('brownfield dominant-proprietary-suite') and cite Microsoft as the common instance. Confidence medium because the term may be deliberately retained as a realistic, named brownfield archetype rather than UL-specific.

proposedGenericDecision: Reframe to refer generically to a future multi-institution consortium / collaborative network rather than a specific 'phase-2 ... network' tied to this particular project roadmap.
rationale: 'phase-2 international university network anticipated by this Reference' ties the text to a specific programme phasing of the originating project (UL/SnT-driven roadmap). surfaceForm: CERN; MIT; Stanford; ETH Zürich; Cambridge; Indiana University; NUS Singapore; USP Brazil; University of Michigan; KU Leuven
location: ul-it-policy/technical/ch01-synthesis-EN.tex § Real-world precedents at a glance (sec:synth-precedents), itemize list lines 512-523
proposedGenericDecision: Retain as named external precedents. These are third-party institutions cited as evidence (Layer-5 institutional precedents), not the document's own institution; naming them is required for the evidence to be verifiable and does NOT bind the document to any single institution.
rationale: Institution-agnosticism concerns the *subject* institution (the adopter), not cited external exemplars. Removing these named precedents would weaken the evidence base and violate the project's evidence methodology (minimum 5 diverse named institutions). They are publicly documented and apply regardless of who adopts the suite. Flagged as explicit named institutions but decision is keep.

surfaceForm: RNP (Latin American research-network integration through RNP); Merit Network; SUNet; UDN (University Data Network); eduGAIN

proposedGenericDecision: Keep RNP/Merit/SUNet/UDN as they are attributes of the named external precedents (verifiable specifics). eduGAIN in the architecture table is a global interoperation standard/federation, not an institution binding; keep.
rationale: These named networks belong to the cited external precedents and are required for those precedents to be verifiable. eduGAIN is a worldwide federation usable by any institution and is the correct generic interoperation reference. None binds the document to the subject institution.
